output.summary: A tender aquatic perennial native to Africa, papyrus forms tall, reed-like stands in shallow water, flooded swamps and lake margins. Its triangular green stems end in dense, feather-duster clusters of fine green rays, and it was historically used to make papyrus paper and boats. The pith of young shoots was eaten cooked or raw.
output.edibilityNote: The pith of young shoots was historically eaten both cooked and raw.
